info.description:
The API of an fvoci server.

## Signing in

`login` answers with a `Set-Cookie` header that carries the session: the cookie `__Host-fvoci_session` where the server is reached over HTTPS, `fvoci_session` over plain HTTP. It is `HttpOnly`, so a page's scripts never see it, and a browser sends it by itself. A client that is no browser may send the cookie's value as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` instead. A few operations that read a shared board need no session when the request has the board's `readToken`.

## Requests that change something

Every request whose method is not `GET` or `HEAD` needs the header `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, unless it has a bearer token, and is refused with 403 and the reason `csrf` without it. If it has an `Origin` header, the origin must be the server's own (or one the server was configured to accept); otherwise it is refused with 403 and the reason `foreign_origin`.

## Answers

An operation answers 200 with a body, 201 with what it made, or 204 with no body. Every other status comes with an `ErrorBody`: `error` names the kind of the refusal and goes with the status, `reason` tells apart causes a client must tell apart, and `field` names the member of the request that was refused. A session that is missing or over is 401. What the user may not see is 404, as if it were not there; what they may see but not do is 403.

The identifiers of users, teams, boards, blocks and categories are UUIDs, written lower-case with hyphens; a client takes every identifier as an opaque string. Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

## Lists

Every list comes in an order, and the description of each operation says which. Where it says nothing else, the order is that of creation, oldest first, and by identifier among what was created in the same millisecond.

## Request bodies

A request schema lists the members a request is for. An optional member may be left out or be `null`. A body with members the schema does not list is not refused for them.
